topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture topic and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer selective advantages that drive clonal expansion in pre-malignant tissues.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and investigate whether tumors initiate from tissue stem cells or committed progenitors using leukemia and intestinal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory drivers of tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how microenvironmental cues, inflammatory signaling, and stromal interactions promote tumor initiation, dedifferentiation, and growth.

topics.label: Experimental technologies for studying tumor architecture and evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes single-cell sequencing and spatial omics methods used to resolve the clonal timing and spatial cellular interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Synthesis of multifactorial cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic integrates genetic alterations, cell of origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified model of Darwinian cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This section marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the upcoming session.
